_readme: Fellowships that are not postdoc jobs: professional and leadership fellowships, visiting research fellowships, institutes for advanced study, journalism and entrepreneurship fellowships. OFFICIAL sources only. Same rules as postdoc.json (statusOverride null|varies|unconfirmed|closed; never invent dates or amounts). kinds: leadership | research | visiting | media | startup. audience: professionals | phd-students | postdocs | senior-researchers | journalists | entrepreneurs. Postdoctoral fellowships live in postdoc.json and are linked from the Fellowships page. Checked weekly — see AGENT.md.

programmes.title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship (Pakistan)
programmes.provider: U.S. Department of State, administered in Pakistan by USEFP
programmes.summary: A ten-month, non-degree programme in the United States for mid-career Pakistani professionals: graduate-level coursework plus professional experience with a U.S. organisation.
programmes.location: U.S. universities (placement by the programme)
programmes.fields: Public-service fields; the 2027 call named AI and cyber-security policy, economic and market development, law and human rights, public health, national and regional security, and natural resource management.
eligibility: Pakistani citizens only; dual U.S./Pakistani nationals are not eligible.
16 years of education (4-year bachelor's, or 2-year bachelor's plus a master's).
8–18 years of progressively responsible professional experience.
Proof of English: a Duolingo score report, unless you hold a valid TOEFL iBT or IELTS score.
A guaranteed job on return and commitment to serving Pakistan.

Not eligible: U.S. graduate-school alumni from the last seven years, people with long-term U.S. experience in the last five years, and university teachers or researchers without management experience.
programmes.nationalities: Pakistani citizens (this Pakistan-specific route; other countries apply through their own Fulbright commission or U.S. embassy).
programmes.funding: Tuition, airfare, textbooks, a living stipend and health insurance.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027 cycle closed on 20 May 2026. USEFP has not yet announced the next call.

procedure: Apply online through the USEFP application portal — paper applications are not accepted.
Upload your English test result and reference letters using USEFP's template.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; the U.S. side makes the final selection and university placement.

verification.notes: From the USEFP Humphrey page (status: closed, deadline 20 May 2026) and the USEFP announcement of the 2027 call.

warnings: The fellowship cannot be deferred and dependants cannot accompany fellows at the start.

programmes.title: Fulbright Scholar Program (Pakistani scholars)
programmes.provider: U.S. Department of State, administered in Pakistan by USEFP
programmes.summary: Up to 10 months of lecturing, postdoctoral research, or both at a U.S. college or university for Pakistani academics and professionals.
programmes.location: A U.S. college or university that invites you
programmes.fields: All disciplines except clinical medicine
eligibility: PhD or terminal degree in your field (the FAQ also allows distinguished leaders in their field).
Not eligible if your PhD was completed within the last two years.
Not eligible if you were in the U.S. for research or long-term education in the last five years, or already hold a work or residence visa in any country.
Excellent written and spoken English (no test required).
At least one invitation letter from a U.S. university, submitted with the application.
programmes.nationalities: Pakistani citizens residing and working in Pakistan.
programmes.funding: Airfare, an incidental research allowance, a living stipend and health insurance; one accompanying dependant is fully covered.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027 program closed on 28 October 2026. Check USEFP for the next call.

procedure: Secure an invitation letter from a U.S. host university.
Submit the online application with three reference letters through the USEFP portal.
Incomplete or paper applications are not considered.

verification.notes: From the USEFP Fulbright Scholar page (status: closed, deadline 28 October 2026).

programmes.title: Nieman Fellowship for Journalists (Harvard)
programmes.provider: Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard University
programmes.summary: A full academic year at Harvard for working journalists to study a topic of their choice, audit classes at Harvard and MIT and take part in Nieman seminars.
programmes.location: Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA
programmes.fields: Journalism in any medium
eligibility: Working journalist with at least five years of full-time media experience (student journalism does not count).
Must speak, read and write English fluently.
Non-U.S. citizens — including those working in the U.S. — apply through the International Nieman Fellowship.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities (international track for non-U.S. citizens).
programmes.funding: A $90,000 stipend paid over nine months, plus a health-insurance supplement (up to $6,250 for the fellow) and a child-care allowance for children 12 and under.

dates.deadlineNote: International deadline 1 December; recommendation letters are due by 15 December. Offers are made in May and the fellowship starts around mid-August.

procedure: Complete the online application: two essays, a professional profile and study-proposal summary, and work samples.
Arrange recommendation letters, submitted through the portal by 15 December.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed on Zoom in April.

verification.notes: Deadlines, stipend and eligibility from the Nieman How to apply page and FAQ.

warnings: The FAQ advises nationals of countries where the U.S. has suspended J-visa issuance to wait before applying, unless they hold a second citizenship from an unaffected country.

programmes.title: Eisenhower Fellowships — Global Program
programmes.provider: Eisenhower Fellowships
programmes.summary: A nearly six-week leadership programme in the United States for established mid-career leaders, built around individual meetings with U.S. counterparts.
programmes.location: United States (in person, with virtual components)
programmes.fields: All sectors
eligibility: Priority to applicants aged 32–45 at the time of the programme.
Citizenship of, or at least five years' residence in, the country you would represent; current U.S. residents are not eligible.
Strong English.
Applicants from countries where the EF network is not active must show regional impact and obtain a recommendation letter from an EF network member.
programmes.nationalities: All countries; priority to countries where the EF network is active — check the eligible-countries list on the EF website.
programmes.funding: Programme costs are covered by EF; spousal travel is not funded. The official eligibility page does not itemise the package.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027 Global Program closed on 15 May 2026. EF says to check back for future application cycles.

procedure: Check that your country is on EF's eligible-countries list (or secure a network recommendation).
Apply online when the next cycle opens.
Selected fellows need employer approval for full-time leave.

verification.notes: From the EF eligibility page and apply page (applications closed).

programmes.title: Rotary Peace Fellowship
programmes.provider: The Rotary Foundation
programmes.summary: Fully funded master's degrees (15–24 months) or a one-year professional certificate in peace and development studies at Rotary Peace Centers.
programmes.location: Master's: Duke & UNC (USA), International Christian University (Japan), University of Bradford (UK), University of Queensland (Australia), Uppsala University (Sweden). Certificate: Makerere (Uganda), Bahçeşehir (Türkiye), Symbiosis (India, from 2027).
programmes.fields: Peace, conflict and development
eligibility: Designed for leaders with work experience in peace and development.
Certificate programme: at least five years of full-time relevant experience and English proficiency.
Not for doctoral study; active Rotary members are not eligible.
Master's alumni and Global Grant scholars must wait three years before the certificate programme.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.funding: Tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transport, and internship and field-study expenses.

dates.deadlineNote: Rotary says the 2028–29 application will be available online in February 2027. Applications are submitted between February and 15 May; the exact 2027 dates are not yet published.

procedure: Choose master's or certificate and rank your preferred centres.
A club or district endorsement is optional but strongly encouraged — contact a local Rotary club early.
Submit the online application in the February–May window; endorser interviews follow in June.

verification.notes: Timeline from the Rotary peace fellowships page; partner universities from the master's and certificate pages.

programmes.title: Commonwealth Professional Fellowships
programmes.provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (FCDO)
programmes.summary: Six weeks to three months at a UK host organisation in your sector for mid-career professionals from low and middle income Commonwealth countries.
programmes.location: UK host organisations selected by the CSC
programmes.fields: Set by each host organisation's programme (development-related themes)
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible low or middle income Commonwealth country — Pakistan is on the list.
At least five years of relevant work experience.
Currently employed at an organisation you will return to.
Apply to a specific host organisation's programme and meet its own criteria.
programmes.nationalities: Low and middle income Commonwealth countries (a separate strand exists for non-ODA countries such as Australia, Canada and Malta).
programmes.funding: Return airfare, visa fee reimbursement, a monthly stipend (£2,104, or £2,612 in London — 2024/25 rates), an arrival allowance and up to £2,000 for agreed courses or UK travel.

dates.deadlineNote: The CSC page lists a closing date of 22 August without a year. Host programmes change every cycle — check the CSC page for the current call.

procedure: Pick a host organisation programme from the CSC list.
Contact the host first if it recruits from an established network.
Apply through the CSC online form — the CSC does not accept applications by other means.

sources.label: CSC — Professional Fellowships: information for candidates

verification.notes: Eligibility and stipend from the CSC candidates page; the page does not state the year of the closing date, so the cycle is marked unconfirmed.

programmes.title: Commonwealth Startup Fellowship
programmes.provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK, with Imperial College London
programmes.summary: A six-month programme for founders of revenue-generating startups from low and middle income Commonwealth countries: online coaching, a bootcamp and a capstone week in London.
programmes.location: Online, with a bootcamp (Accra, Ghana) and capstone week (London, UK)
programmes.fields: Startups from all sectors
eligibility: At least a graduate-level qualification; fluent English.
Citizen of (or refugee from) an eligible low or middle income Commonwealth country and permanently resident there — Pakistan is on the list.
A legally registered startup with at least 12 months of operation, paying customers and a sustainable (not donation-based) model.
Not a Commonwealth Professional Fellow in the last five years.
programmes.nationalities: Low and middle income Commonwealth countries.
programmes.funding: Travel, accommodation and catering for the bootcamp and London capstone week, visa fee reimbursement, and up to £2,000 in equity-free grants.

dates.deadlineNote: The cohort starting November 2026 closed on 1 September 2026. The next call has not been announced.

procedure: Apply through the CSC online portal (applications cannot be edited after submission).
Include business and team details, two referees, a one-minute video pitch and a passport or ID scan.

sources.label: GOV.UK — UK opens scholarships and startup fellowships for Pakistan

verification.notes: From the CSC candidates page (applications closed) and the British High Commission announcement (3 August – 1 September 2026).

programmes.title: Chevening Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies Fellowship
programmes.provider: UK FCDO (Chevening) and the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies
programmes.summary: Five months of self-directed research at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies for mid-career academics and professionals.
programmes.location: Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies, Oxford, UK
programmes.fields: The culture and civilisation of Islam and contemporary Muslim societies
eligibility: Citizen of and resident in an eligible country — Pakistan is on the list.
A postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience).
At least five years of professional and/or academic research experience.
Meet Chevening's general criteria (leadership potential).
programmes.nationalities: Listed countries only, including Pakistan.
programmes.funding: Living expenses, return economy airfare and an allowance for research-related activities.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027–28 call closed on 6 October 2026. Chevening calls usually open in August — check chevening.org.

procedure: Apply online through chevening.org when the call opens.
First interview with the British High Commission; final interview with OCIS.

verification.notes: Eligibility and benefits from the Chevening OCIS page (closed); the 6 October 2026 closing date from Chevening's awards list.

programmes.title: Reuters Institute Journalist Fellowship (Oxford)
programmes.provider: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
programmes.summary: Three or six months at Oxford for working journalists to work on a project for their newsroom or the news industry, with seminars and a global cohort.
programmes.location: Oxford, UK
programmes.fields: Journalism; a climate-journalism strand also runs
eligibility: More than five years' experience working in newsrooms.
You must plan to return to journalism after the fellowship.
programmes.nationalities: Journalists from all regions.
programmes.funding: Fully funded fellowships are available (for example the Thomson Reuters Fellowship); amounts are not published on the page.

dates.deadlineNote: Applications reopen in January 2027; applicants hear back by mid-May. The exact deadline is not yet published.

procedure: Prepare a project proposal relevant to your newsroom or the industry.
Apply online when the call reopens in January.

sources.label: Reuters Institute — Our journalist fellowship programme

verification.notes: From the Reuters Institute How to apply page (closed for 2026–27, reopening January 2027).

programmes.title: International Climate Protection Fellowship
programmes.provider: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
programmes.summary: A climate-protection project in Germany with a host you choose, for prospective leaders and postdocs from non-European developing and transition countries.
programmes.location: Host institutions anywhere in Germany
programmes.fields: Climate protection and climate-relevant resource conservation
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible non-European developing or transition country and predominantly living and working there — Pakistan is on the Humboldt country lists.
First degree completed within the last twelve years.
Prospective leaders: at least 24 months of relevant climate work experience after the first degree (or a master's plus 12 months), and initial leadership experience.
Postdocs: a climate-related doctorate no more than four years old, with peer-reviewed publications.
Very good English and/or German; a German host who agrees your project.
programmes.nationalities: Non-European developing and transition countries (see the Humboldt country list).
programmes.funding: Prospective leaders €2,500, €2,800 or €3,000 a month; postdocs €3,000 a month, plus ancillary benefits and a host allowance.

dates.deadlineNote: The next call opens on 7 December 2026 and has no fixed closing date: it closes once 120 applications are received (90 prospective leaders, 30 postdocs). Register in advance and apply early. Host statements are due by 1 March.

procedure: Register on the Humboldt website in advance — you are emailed when the call opens.
Agree your project with a host in Germany (the foundation does not find hosts).
Submit the online form with a motivation letter, project proposal, CV, language and degree certificates.
Two referees upload letters; your host uploads a statement and mentoring agreement.

sources.label: Humboldt Foundation — International Climate Protection Fellowship
Humboldt Foundation — travel lump sums by country (lists Pakistan)

verification.notes: Call dates, amounts and eligibility from the Humboldt programme page.

warnings: The call closes as soon as the application cap is reached — there may be very little time after 7 December.

programmes.title: Georg Forster Research Fellowship
programmes.provider: Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
programmes.summary: Research stays in Germany for researchers from developing and transition countries. Currently suspended — listed here so you know not to apply.
programmes.location: Germany
programmes.fields: All disciplines (research relevant to sustainable development)
eligibility: Applications are no longer accepted — see the warning.
Previously: citizens of developing or transition countries (excluding China and India) with a recent doctorate and peer-reviewed publications.
programmes.nationalities: Developing and transition countries (excluding China and India) — programme suspended.
programmes.funding: Previously €3,000 a month (postdocs) or €3,600 (experienced researchers).

dates.deadlineNote: The Humboldt Foundation stopped accepting applications with immediate effect because of budget cuts and is designing a new programme. The foundation suggests the Humboldt Research Fellowship instead (see our Postdoc section).

procedure: Do not apply — consider the Humboldt Research Fellowship or the International Climate Protection Fellowship instead.

sources.label: Humboldt Foundation — Georg Forster Research Fellowship

verification.notes: The official page states that applications can no longer be accepted.

warnings: Suspended: the Humboldt Foundation is not accepting applications for this fellowship.

programmes.title: ICTP Associates Programme (Junior, Regular, Senior)
programmes.provider: Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)
programmes.summary: A six-year appointment that lets scientists working in developing countries make repeat research visits to ICTP in Trieste, with travel paid.
programmes.location: ICTP, Trieste, Italy
programmes.fields: ICTP research areas — high-energy physics, condensed matter, mathematics, earth system physics, quantitative life sciences and more
eligibility: A PhD and a main affiliation with a scientific institute in a developing country.
Junior Associates: up to age 35; Regular Associates: 36–45; Senior Associates: 46–65 (age at application).
Two recommendation letters from senior scientists, preferably from another institute.
programmes.nationalities: Scientists working in developing countries (eligibility follows your institute, not your passport).
programmes.funding: Junior and Regular: three travel fares, for three visits of 30–60 days each (180 days over six years). The pages do not state a separate living allowance — check with ICTP.

dates.deadlineNote: Apply through ICTP's online application system by 31 January 2027.

procedure: Apply online via the 'Apply now' link on the ICTP page for your age band.
Enter your two referees in the portal so they can upload letters.
Questions: assoc@ictp.it.

verification.notes: Deadline 31 January 2027 and visit rules from the ICTP Junior and Regular Associates pages.

programmes.title: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan
programmes.provider: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS)
programmes.summary: Invites experienced overseas researchers to Japan for collaborative research (long-term) or discussions and lectures (short-term). Your Japanese host applies for you.
programmes.location: Universities and research institutions in Japan
programmes.fields: All fields
eligibility: Overseas researchers with an excellent record of research achievement.
You need a host researcher in Japan, who submits the application through their institution.
programmes.nationalities: Overseas researchers (no single nationality restriction on the schedule page).
programmes.funding: Round-trip airfare; long-term: maintenance allowance ¥387,600 a month and up to ¥150,000 research support; short-term: ¥18,000 a day; overseas travel insurance.

dates.deadlineNote: Deadline for the host institution to submit to JSPS: 23 April 2027 (5 p.m. JST), for arrivals from October 2027 to March 2028. Host institutions set earlier internal deadlines. The FY2028 long-term round is usually due in late August.

procedure: Agree a collaboration with a host researcher in Japan.
Your host prepares and submits the application via their institution in the JSPS electronic system.
JSPS publishes results about three months after the deadline.

verification.notes: Schedule from the JSPS application page; allowances from the JSPS program page and JSPS San Francisco office.

warnings: You cannot apply yourself — the application comes from your host in Japan.

programmes.title: Japan Foundation Japanese Studies Fellowship
programmes.provider: The Japan Foundation
programmes.summary: Research stays in Japan for scholars and PhD candidates in the humanities and social sciences working on Japan-related topics.
programmes.location: Japan (with an affiliation you arrange)
programmes.fields: Humanities and social sciences related to Japan (comparative research included); not natural sciences, medicine or engineering
eligibility: Doctoral candidates who have completed coursework (stays of 4–12 months).
Researchers with a PhD or equivalent professional experience (21–89 days or 4–12 months).
Citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan, living there.
Proficient in Japanese or English; affiliation arranged by the deadline.
programmes.nationalities: Countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (U.S. applicants use a separate New York procedure).
programmes.funding: A round-trip airline ticket plus a stipend and allowances (monthly amounts are in the full application guidelines).
programmes.duration: 21 days to 12 months, depending on category

dates.deadlineNote: Apply through the Online Application Portal by 1 p.m. Japan time on 1 December 2026. Results in April 2027.

procedure: Arrange an affiliation with a Japanese institution.
Submit form RJS-FW through the Japan Foundation Online Application Portal.
Southeast Asian applicants use the separate JF-JSA-ASEAN programme.

sources.label: Japan Foundation — Fellowship programme outline FY2027 (PDF)

verification.notes: From the FY2027 programme outline and the Japan Foundation programme page.

programmes.title: Korea Foundation Fellowship for Field Research
programmes.provider: Korea Foundation
programmes.summary: One to six months of on-site field research in Korea for doctoral candidates and faculty abroad working on Korea-related topics.
programmes.location: Korea, with a Korean affiliate scholar and host institution you arrange
programmes.fields: Korean studies and Korea-related humanities and social sciences
eligibility: Type A: doctoral candidates writing their dissertation; Type B: full-time lecturers or professors.
Citizenship or permanent residency outside Korea.
Research in Korean or English; no KF or other Korean public field-research funding in the last 3 years.
programmes.nationalities: Scholars based outside Korea.
programmes.funding: KRW 2,300,000 a month (doctoral candidates) or KRW 3,000,000 (faculty), a one-time entry allowance, travel insurance, and round-trip airfare for residents of OECD-DAC ODA recipient countries (upper-middle income excluded). No accommodation.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027 call ran from 19 August to 14 October 2026. The next call has not been announced.

procedure: Arrange a Korean affiliate scholar and host institution.
Apply through the KF Online Application Portal (apply.kf.or.kr).

sources.label: Korean Cultural Center (Korean government) — 2027 KF Fellowship for Field Research

verification.notes: Taken from the 2027 call published by the Korean Cultural Center; the KF portal itself requires login.

programmes.title: TÜBİTAK 2221 Fellowships for Visiting Scientists and Scientists on Sabbatical
programmes.provider: TÜBİTAK (Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye)
programmes.summary: Funds visiting and sabbatical scientists to carry out research, teaching or workshops at universities and institutes in Türkiye. Your Turkish host applies for you.
programmes.location: Universities and public research institutions in Türkiye
programmes.fields: All fields
eligibility: A doctoral degree (PhD certificate required).
If working abroad in a doctoral-level position: at least 4 years of work experience.
Sabbatical category: a leave letter that explicitly says sabbatical.
No more than 12 months of support in the last 3 years.
programmes.nationalities: No nationality requirement on the official page.
programmes.funding: Up to 81,000 TL a month (visiting) or 105,000 TL (sabbatical), round-trip airfare bought by TÜBİTAK, and health insurance support for stays of 3–12 months.
programmes.duration: Short-term 7 days – 3 months; long-term and sabbatical 3–12 months

dates.deadlineNote: The host scientist submits by 17:30 on 30 November 2026. TÜBİTAK runs four terms a year; the 2027 dates are not yet published.

procedure: Find a host scientist (PhD, full-time at a Turkish university or public institution).
Your host applies online through TYBS with an e-signature, including a work plan in Turkish.
Apply in the term before your planned arrival.

verification.notes: 2026 application terms, stipends and rules from the TÜBİTAK 2221 page.

warnings: You cannot apply yourself — the application comes from your host in Türkiye.

programmes.title: IIASA Young Scientists Summer Program (YSSP)
programmes.provider: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA)
programmes.summary: A three-month summer research project at IIASA near Vienna for PhD students working on global environmental, economic and social change.
programmes.location: IIASA, Laxenburg (near Vienna), Austria
programmes.fields: Topics linked to IIASA research groups (systems analysis, energy, climate, population, food, water and more)
eligibility: Enrolled in a PhD programme, ideally within one to two years of completing it.
A research topic that fits an IIASA research group.
Available full-time and in person for the whole programme.
programmes.nationalities: PhD students from around the world; grants are mainly from IIASA's National Member Organizations for their own nationals.
programmes.funding: Member-organisation grants are usually €1,700 a month plus airfare. Applicants from non-member countries must find other funds; IIASA has limited funds for exceptional non-member candidates.
programmes.duration: 3 months (plus one month to finish the report)

dates.deadlineNote: Apply through Onlyfy by 10 January 2027, 23:00 CET. Contact your chosen research group with a half-page outline before writing the full proposal.

procedure: Choose up to two IIASA research groups and send them a half-page outline and CV.
Write the research proposal and prepare one PDF with CV, motivation letter and publications.
Submit everything on Onlyfy in one session (progress cannot be saved) with two referees.

verification.notes: Deadline and steps from the IIASA application page; funding from the IIASA funding page.

warnings: Funding is not guaranteed — check whether your country has an IIASA member organisation offering YSSP grants before you rely on one.

programmes.title: NIAS Individual Fellowship
programmes.provider: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study (NIAS-KNAW)
programmes.summary: Five or ten months in Amsterdam to work on your own humanities or social-science project in an interdisciplinary community, with places reserved for Global South scholars.
programmes.location: NIAS, Amsterdam
programmes.fields: Humanities and social sciences (broadly)
eligibility: At least three years of academic experience after the PhD (counted to the call's closing date).
A permanent academic post is not required.
Fluent English; full-time on site four days a week.
Applicants affiliated outside the EU compete in a separate category (up to 72 places).
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities; category depends on your institutional affiliation.
programmes.funding: Described on NIAS's 'What NIAS offers' page; amounts are not stated on the call page.

dates.deadlineNote: The call opens on 15 January 2027 and closes on 15 March 2027 at 12:00 noon CET. NIAS assesses at most 216 eligible applications — apply early.

procedure: Submit the online form with a project proposal, CV with key publications and three suggested international reviewers.
Answer two questions on interdisciplinary and community engagement.
All eligible applicants hear by 15 December 2027.

verification.notes: Call dates and eligibility from the NIAS Individual Fellowship page.

programmes.title: IAS CEU Global Invisible University Fellowships
programmes.provider: Institute for Advanced Study at Central European University
programmes.summary: Residential research fellowships in Budapest for senior and promising young scholars in the social sciences and humanities, with a stipend and guesthouse accommodation.
programmes.location: Budapest site of Central European University, Hungary
programmes.fields: Social sciences and humanities, linked to themes such as democratisation, inequality, human rights and climate justice
eligibility: Highly accomplished senior scholars and promising young scholars.
A project related to at least one of the programme's thematic areas.
Fluent English.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.funding: A monthly stipend (amount not stated on the call page) and accommodation at the Raoul Wallenberg Guesthouse.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027–28 call closed on 1 October 2026. The next call has not been announced.

procedure: Apply online when the next call opens; choose the fellowship category and residential period.

verification.notes: From the call published on the NetIAS network site; stipend amount not stated.

programmes.title: FIAS Fellowships — French Institutes for Advanced Study
programmes.provider: French Institutes for Advanced Study (RFIEA)
programmes.summary: Ten-month research residencies at seven French institutes for advanced study (Paris, Lyon, Aix-Marseille, Nantes, Montpellier, Cergy, Orléans-Tours).
programmes.location: Seven institutes for advanced study in France
programmes.fields: Social sciences and humanities, plus interdisciplinary research
eligibility: PhD plus at least 2 years of research experience (PhD training does not count).
Not more than 12 months in France in the three years before the deadline.
All countries and career levels from postdoc to senior.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.funding: €2,200 a month living allowance, accommodation, social security, travel and a research and training budget.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027–28 call (29 fellowships) closed on 25 June 2026. Check fias-fp.eu for the next call.

procedure: Apply online at fias-fp.eu when the call opens; study the priorities of each host institute first.

verification.notes: Terms of the 2027–28 call from NetIAS and the Paris IAS.

programmes.title: NNF-IAS Fellowships on Health and Sustainability (Nordic)
programmes.provider: Nordic Institutes for Advanced Studies, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation
programmes.summary: Two-year salaried fellowships at institutes for advanced study in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark for researchers working on health and sustainability.
programmes.location: HCAS (Helsinki), CAS (Oslo), SCAS (Uppsala) and AIAS (Aarhus, Denmark)
programmes.fields: Any discipline, within the call's health-and-sustainability theme
eligibility: Any nationality; 2–10 years of experience after the PhD.
Not mainly resident in the host country for more than 12 months in the two years before the deadline.
Willing to live in the host country for the whole fellowship.
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.funding: A full-time salary by host-country rules, travel and relocation support, and a research budget of up to €20,000.

dates.deadlineNote: The first call (theme: inequity in health) closed on 1 October 2026. Three more calls are planned; dates and themes are not yet published.

procedure: Apply to the next call and rank your preferred host institute.

verification.notes: From the University of Helsinki call page.

programmes.title: Max Weber Fellowships (European University Institute)
programmes.provider: European University Institute (EUI)
programmes.summary: One- or two-year postdoctoral fellowships in Florence for recent PhDs in economics, history, law, and political and social sciences, with training in teaching, publishing and grant writing.
programmes.location: European University Institute, Florence (Badia Fiesolana), Italy
programmes.fields: Economics, history, law, political and social sciences
eligibility: Within five years of completing your PhD; any nationality.
Preference for those who have just finished their doctorate and have not held a postdoctoral fellowship.
Not eligible if you are at the EUI at the deadline (doctoral programme, employment or fellowship).
programmes.nationalities: All nationalities.
programmes.funding: €2,500 a month plus family allowances where applicable, health insurance and a personal research and mission fund of €1,500; an optional second-year teaching contract adds about €850 net a month.
programmes.duration: 1 or 2 years, depending on the academic unit

dates.deadlineNote: The general deadline (16 October 2026) has passed. Late applications are accepted only for the Department of Economics until 1 March 2027, 14:00 CET. Fellowships start on 1 September 2027.

procedure: Apply through the EUI online application portal.
Register early and enter your referees so they can submit letters before the deadline.
